attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, in the first person.

semantics.note: This is a retrospective claim that Duplex had not moved much past its narrow salon and restaurant demo by Sept 2022. The normalised proposition keeps the 'so far' scope.

contract.note: Nothing in the wording sets a threshold for 'a whole lot further'. The contract's plain reading counts deployment, new telephone tasks and better automation as progress, and does not require general conversation. That is a fair, ordinary reading of 'demo stage'.

evidence.note: 2018 announcement. It sets the baseline: closed domains only, no general conversation, and business-hours calls were already in scope.

Google, Oct 2020: over a million completed bookings, millions of business-info updates across eight countries, and 99% of calls fully automated. This is deployment well beyond a demo, but it is a company disclosure.
Google, Sept 2020: Hold for Me, a new Duplex-powered phone function. It launched only as a limited Pixel preview in the US.

reviews.rationale: By 2020 Duplex had been deployed at scale, ran with high automation, and had picked up an extra phone use (Hold for Me). That meets the contract's contradiction condition, even though the capability was still limited to closed domains. The caveat is that the figures come only from Google's own disclosures, though the contract accepts these as sources.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: The claim is a universal historical one about every claimed compositionality solution up to Sept 2022. The normalisation keeps the 'every' quantifier.

contract.note: The contract separates success on a restricted benchmark from a broad solution, and that is fair given the surrounding discussion. Which systems count as 'proposed solutions' is left unspecified.

evidence.note: 2017 SCAN experiments: recurrent networks fail badly at systematic generalization. This supports the claim only for the models tested, not every proposed solution.

Feb 2022 COGS results: compositional parsers keep high accuracy at deeper recursion. This challenges the literal 'never master' wording, but it is a restricted task and falls short of the contract's breadth requirement.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows some systems failing (e1) and a robust success on one restricted task (e2). The support condition needs a fairly complete record of proposed solutions, and the packet has none. The contradiction condition needs broad reliable generalization, which e2 does not show. Neither condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assessment in his own post.

semantics.note: In context, 'won't change that' judges the evidence available in Sept 2022; it is not an open-ended forecast. 'Giant' is emphasis. The testable core is that the cited demo did not show compositionality was solved.

contract.note: Treating 'won't' as a judgement about current evidence fits the surrounding passage, and the Sept 2022 window is a reasonable reading.

evidence.note: Alexander's 2025 retrospective, published before the evaluation date. It reports that the evaluators accepted only 1 of the 5 Sept 2022 Imagen prompts. This is his account, not the original scoring records.
Google's May 2022 DrawBench results show human raters preferred Imagen over other models. That shows relative progress, not a reliable general solution, and it predates the target window.

reviews.rationale: The Sept 2022 five-prompt demo was scored 1/5 by independent evaluators. Google's own evidence shows Imagen was preferred over rivals, not that it reliably handled compositional generalization. So the cited demo and announcement did not establish a general solution, and the claim holds for that period.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement. He summarises the Winoground paper, but the factual assertion is his.

semantics.note: 'Should be a piece of cake' is rhetoric. The checkable part is that popular vision-language models failed word-order caption matching, and the normalisation captures that.

contract.note: Using Winoground as the test is fair because Marcus names it himself. The contract separates text, image and group scores.

evidence.note: Winoground paper, April 2022: models were close to or below chance, and every model fell below random chance on the group score. Some text scores beat chance but sat about 50 points below humans.

reviews.rationale: The contemporary Winoground evaluation found widespread near-chance or below-chance results. Every model scored below chance on the group score, which requires all comparisons to be correct. That meets the support condition for the 2022 period up to the post.
